title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: ancient Semi-Pelagians owned the sequitur — Faustus on free choice
pass_a_gloss: The ancient Semi-Pelagians saw that this necessarily follows from the aforesaid opinion, and therefore, as if it had nothing absurd in itself, taught this openly. So Faustus, On Free Choice, book 1: The state of man into diverse things can turn not according to the constitution of God, but according to the liberty of choice. And book 1, chapter 20: What God ought to foreknow and preordain concerning us, as far as pertains to the future, consists in the progress and defect of man.
pass_b_english: The old Semi-Pelagians saw that sequitur and taught it openly as no absurdity. Faustus (On Free Choice 1): a man's state can turn this way or that not by God's constitution but by free choice. And 1.20: what God is to foreknow and preordain about us for the future consists in man's progress or failure.
source_text: Antiqui Semipelagiani viderunt hoc necessario sequi ex praedicta sententia, atque idcirco tanquam nihil absurdi in se haberet, hoc palam docuerunt. Sic Faustus De lib. arbit. lib. 1. Status hominis in diversa, non pro constitutione Dei, sed pro arbitrii libertate potest versari. Et libro 1. cap. 20. Quid de nobis praescire ac praeordinare debeat Deus, quantum pertinet ad futurum, in profectu hominis defectuque consistit.
